chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Hope for a resurgence of big bands from the schools
summary: Herman hopes the best bands in American history come from today's students and that youth will force the record industry and radio to listen.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Can you foresee what the music business might be like with, say, multiplying that force of young talent coming out by five to ten times?

Well, I would hope -- now, this is a specific hope, I would hope and pray and love to believe with all my heart that because of this phenomenal rise in the interest in music that we'll have some of the best bands and groups to ever be in the history of American music, out of this whole grouping that are still in the educational process as students.

I would hope that there's a resurgent and a complete rejuvenation of a big band scene. And it can only come from this whole educational process, nowhere else. But they will also have to fight for the same things we fought for a hundred years ago, and that is how you get the record industry to appreciate us, to do something about us.
How do you get radio to play our performance? How do you get anyone to move for us? We're the best that we've ever produced in this country, and we need that help.

And I'm depending completely on the spirit and the spunk and everything that says determination by American youth. Because these are the best players we've ever produced, and I have fear -- I really -- I hope with a desperation, but I also have belief that they have the courage and guts and conviction to say, 'Hey, baby, move over, we're coming in.' I'd be glad to carry the flag in front of that group, baby, believe me.
